findings.title: Shared PWA API cache crosses account/authorization boundaries
findings.implementation: Network-only API policy precedes asset matchers; activation deletes legacy API/static/image caches and navigation excludes every API path.
findings.verification: Real generated production worker in isolated Chrome: synthetic admin→viewer→anonymous headers, offline and 11-second upstream delay, old cache deletion, no API entries. Delays may fail transport; never fall back to privileged data.

findings.title: User-controlled highlight channel IDs escape the recording directory and reach recursive deletion
findings.implementation: Ingress rejects path-like IDs; recorder directories use opaque server-generated names; every destructive cleanup enforces resolved non-root containment.
findings.verification: Actual route/JSON tests reject traversal before process creation; temporary/synthetic recorder tests preserve sibling sentinels and cover failed, slow, cancelled and later-dead startup. Destructive demonstrations were mocked.

findings.title: Public logo requests and async media routes synchronously fetch upstream feeds, blocking every request on the event loop
findings.implementation: Entire synchronous feed lookup/parsing runs in bounded executor workers; refresh locks share work, with cold-failure and stale-cache backoff.
findings.verification: A blocked public logo lookup allows concurrent real ASGI health requests; 20 cold callers share one failure. MEDIA-11 verifies populated-cache backoff/recovery; authoritative media resolver also offloads lookup.

findings.title: Authenticated media calls admit unlimited FFmpeg processes and encoding jobs
findings.implementation: Shared per-worker global/user admission precedes process creation or export work; owned cancellations/failures/dead recorders release capacity.
findings.verification: Mocked concurrent admissions enforce 429 without spawning/queuing excess; duplicate sessions stay within configured budgets; dead/cancelled/failing work is reclaimed. Defaults: 8 processes/2 per user, 2 exports/1 per user.

findings.title: Empty channel ID preserves a client-supplied URL as FFmpeg input
findings.implementation: Channel/source/type/URL come from authoritative catalogs for selection, highlight and Cast; unresolved IDs never preserve request-supplied URLs; FFmpeg protocols constrained.
findings.verification: Empty/whitespace/unknown/off-catalog and provider-failure tests prevent subprocess input from client URLs; valid Dispatcharr and Ersatz sources still resolve under permission checks.

findings.title: Empty signing key passes startup and permits forged administrator tokens
findings.implementation: Startup rejects public, blank, whitespace and fewer than 32 non-padding-character JWT keys before media side effects.
findings.verification: Startup matrix covers login flags and explicit environment JWT_SECRET=; strong synthetic signing configuration succeeds.

findings.title: Explicitly empty local passwords authenticate despite the startup warning
findings.implementation: Empty/unset passwords disable each local account; root/backend examples use blank disabled accounts and require generated signing keys.
findings.verification: None/empty configured admin and viewer passwords reject empty submissions; independently configured viewer login works while admin remains disabled.

findings.title: Full bearer credentials are written to routine request logs
findings.implementation: Central backend/browser logging redacts bearer/query/structured secrets, percent-encoded keys and exception values; traceback local dumps disabled.
findings.verification: Actual Uvicorn HTTP HLS-shaped requests and WebSocket handshakes captured in pretty/JSON logs; synthetic logger tests cover args/nested fields/exceptions and all browser levels/HLS/Cast URLs. Reverse-proxy logs remain operator-owned.

findings.title: Documented local startup sends API requests to the wrong port
findings.implementation: All frontend API clients share relative /api; examples and root/backend/frontend setup docs match backend 8001 and Vite proxy, including signing-key setup.
findings.verification: 38 focused API checks plus actual Chrome with real Vite proxy and synthetic auth/guide fixtures on loopback and machine LAN address; no frontend dotenv. Same machine LAN-origin test, not a separate physical device.

findings.title: Live HLS playlists and segments are cached under the API fallback policy
findings.implementation: Uses FE-01 shared network-only policy; adds dedicated generated-worker coverage for live manifests, segments and Cast HLS.
findings.verification: Actual Chrome verifies all three media route families never enter Cache Storage; offline fetch fails and delayed fetch never serves old media.

findings.title: QR authentication survives cancellation/unmount and can authenticate the abandoned flow
findings.implementation: Attempt generations own PIN creation, serial polls and timers; cancel/retry/timeout/unmount invalidate every late continuation.
findings.verification: Deferred creation and poll tests cover all abandonment paths and replacement ownership; slow polling stays serial and success fires at most once.

findings.title: A stale 401 response logs out a newly signed-in account
findings.implementation: Auth generation accompanies each request; a 401 logs out only its still-current session, including same-token reuse.
findings.verification: Deferred old-account 401 preserves replacement login; current-session 401 logs out; reused-token generation regression passes.

findings.title: Live Channel 0 stops following backend channel changes when ErsatzTV is absent
findings.implementation: Live selection reconciles backend changes directly; optional-catalog failure keeps live controls; populated-catalog default selection waits for loading.
findings.verification: Routed TVView with real stores/sidebar and mocked player adapter: empty and rejected 503 catalogs follow A→B→clear; asynchronous populated catalog retains documented default.

findings.title: Highlight trimming/WebM export downloads a different capture from the preview
findings.implementation: Trim/conversion uploads the held preview bytes to a bounded authenticated export endpoint instead of recapturing the ring.
findings.verification: Modal tests cover delayed trimmed MP4/WebM and untrimmed preview; actual synthetic FFmpeg red/green source conversion and decoded-frame checks prove original capture identity.

findings.title: Cast controls forget a connected, playing receiver after player remount
findings.implementation: Hook initialization reads existing receiver session/media state; remounted controls expose playing/paused state and Stop.
findings.verification: Actual hook and CastButton integrated with SDK doubles exercise playing/paused receiver remounts. No physical Chromecast was used.

findings.title: Cast backend sessions lose ownership on replacement and disconnect races
findings.implementation: Generation-owned backend UUIDs and serialized receiver loads handle replacement, disconnect, pending creation and already-issued loads; debug path shares ownership.
findings.verification: Deferred SDK/process-API fixtures cover replacement, stop/unmount, late creation/load and listener ownership; no actual receiver claim.

findings.title: Player keyboard shortcuts hijack native focused controls
findings.implementation: Both player modes use the shared keyboard hook, preserving focused native and accessible controls.
findings.verification: Native button/link/select, contenteditable and Radix/control targets retain default handling; standalone shortcuts still work. Tests use jsdom, not a TV remote.

findings.title: Sustained WebSocket outage permanently disconnects the UI without a recovery control
findings.implementation: Visible reconnect and browser online/visibility recovery resume exhausted sockets; auth-terminal close and logout remain terminal.
findings.verification: Fake sockets exhaust retries, recover by visible action/online transition without reload, and do not reconnect after logout or 4001.

findings.title: Chat silently discards the draft when the socket cannot send
findings.implementation: Matching server acknowledgement clears the pending draft exactly once; disconnected/timeout/old-socket ACKs preserve it and GIF selection.
findings.verification: Real ChatPanel+hook fixtures and backend ACK route tests cover CONNECTING/CLOSING/CLOSED, pending sends, new edits, rejected/duplicate/late ACKs and lost ACK. ACK means accepted into server memory and broadcast, not durable delivery/read receipts.

findings.title: FFmpeg stderr pipes are never drained, eventually freezing recording/transcoding
findings.implementation: Both FFmpeg services direct stderr/stdout to DEVNULL and use start_new_session, avoiding unread pipe backpressure.
findings.verification: Actual harmless child emits 1 MiB stderr and reaches its progress marker; service stop terminates/reaps it. This is a real process test, not a live media stress test.

findings.title: Concurrent highlight exports share mutable input/output files and can delete each other's results
findings.implementation: Lifecycle-locked snapshots pause the producer briefly, copy completed segments to unique export workspaces, then resume; encoders are cancellation-owned.
findings.verification: Concurrent distinct trim/format jobs keep independent bytes despite ring overwrite and recorder stop; failures/timeouts/cancellation remove workspaces; actual harmless encoder cancellation is reaped.

findings.title: ErsatzTV lookup failure disables independent Dispatcharr highlights and cast
findings.implementation: Authoritative Dispatcharr matches bypass ErsatzTV entirely; true catalog miss is 404, unavailable catalogs yield 503.
findings.verification: Controlled Dispatcharr lineup plus cold Ersatz failure still permits highlight/Cast resolution; genuine missing IDs and provider failures return distinct statuses.

findings.title: HLS rewriting misses URI-bearing tags and playlists with query strings
findings.implementation: All URI-bearing tags route through proxy; playlist detection uses parsed paths with explicit resource/playlist tag semantics and full final-URL resolution.
findings.verification: Round trips cover KEY,MAP,MEDIA,I-FRAME,query variants and query-only MAP. Actual Chrome+hls.js plays generated fMP4(56 decoded frames) and encrypted TS(55); keys/init/audio/subtitles/nested playlists use authenticated proxy, with no direct upstream browser requests.

findings.title: Manifest and logo fetches remain unbounded despite the segment-size cap
findings.implementation: Decoded manifest/logo/feed bodies have byte and time budgets; manifest MIME/header validation rejects wrong resource types; retained legacy helpers use bounded validated redirects.
findings.verification: 138 focused upstream/router/parser checks include false/absent lengths, chunk overflow closure, total async body timeout, bounded synchronous feed reads and video MIME rejected before body reads.

findings.title: Public logo proxy trusts feed-supplied targets and serves arbitrary active content on the application origin
findings.implementation: Logos require configured trusted origins at every hop and matching safe raster signatures/MIME; responses add sandbox CSP and nosniff.
findings.verification: Off-origin metadata makes no request; hostile redirect, HTML/script SVG and mislabeled content are rejected; explicitly allowed raster CDN content works. PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP supported; SVG intentionally refused.

findings.title: Mid-segment upstream failures are silently finalized as successful truncated responses
findings.implementation: Mid-body upstream I/O errors propagate through ASGI so framing aborts; finally closes both upstream response/client.
findings.verification: Injected partial-media then ReadError makes iterator and actual ASGI client fail, rather than completing a truncated 200; resources are closed.

findings.title: Failed EPG refreshes serialize one new timeout per waiting caller instead of sharing the failure
findings.implementation: Refresh success expiry and failed-attempt retry deadlines are separate; populated stale results and cold failures share bounded backoff.
findings.verification: 20 expired-cache callers share one failed attempt; calls during backoff return stale data without network waits; after deadline a successful refresh resets retry state.

findings.title: Concurrent releases can deploy older code after newer code
findings.implementation: Host flock covers source-ancestry acceptance, atomic compose install and verification; unique staging and no latest promotion prevent overlapping stale deployments.
findings.verification: Independent temporary-directory process interleaving proves serialization and delayed A after B is rejected. Does not rely on unverified Gitea concurrency syntax; no host deployment performed.

findings.title: Rebuilding a release reuses a tag that Compose may never pull
findings.implementation: Builds get unique IDs; CI deploys registry digest, explicitly pulls it, verifies running image reference/ID and records previous artifacts.
findings.verification: Orchestration fixtures validate digest/version checks; actual local Docker builds two images with same source marker and verifies first→second→first rollback with distinct image IDs. Remote registry/deploy unexecuted.

findings.title: Channel control bypasses the existing stale-administrator check
findings.implementation: Channel-control guard shares current-admin predicate and applies viewer-selection policy after demotion.
findings.verification: ASGI admin/channel requests deny stale admin with viewer selection off, allow channel selection under viewer policy, and preserve current local/Plex list/owner/default admin cases.

findings.title: A viewer can poison presence data and disable the administrator user list
findings.implementation: Discriminated bounded WebSocket schemas validate JSON before presence/nickname/chat mutation.
findings.verification: Malformed top-level and object/list/numeric/null/string cases cannot poison admin active-users; valid bounded presence and messages still work.

findings.title: An established WebSocket remains authorized after its JWT expires
findings.implementation: Signed expiry bounds the whole WebSocket session, including idle/initial sends; expiry closes 4001 and cleans all ownership state.
findings.verification: Actual short-lived signed-token ASGI tests plus controlled idle/active transports verify expiry, rejected reuse, no later messages/broadcasts, and presence/connection/nickname cleanup.

findings.title: A broadcast timeout silently strands an otherwise live client
findings.implementation: Failed broadcasts remove/close clients and cancel their owning endpoint when transport close cannot unblock receive.
findings.verification: Timed-out transport closes 1011 and cleans once; healthy peers continue; dropped clients receive no future broadcasts and overlapping drops do not duplicate cleanup.

findings.title: Unexpected upstream status payloads crash the whole combined status endpoint
findings.implementation: Status clients validate upstream shapes; decode/schema errors become typed service errors and aggregation preserves healthy peers.
findings.verification: Controlled HTML200, object-for-list, malformed sessions and invalid Dispatcharr field cases plus admin route tests retain the independent healthy-service result.

findings.title: Now-playing and presence metadata do not advance at programme boundaries
findings.implementation: A shared minute clock updates programme/header/presence and independently refreshes live guide data at boundaries with bounded polling.
findings.verification: Routed fake-clock tests cross programme boundaries without unrelated events and update header, presence and live EPG; optional catalog is not required.

findings.title: Trending GIF cache ignores the requested limit
findings.implementation: Trending cache identity includes normalized requested limit and its pagination result.
findings.verification: Both 1→50→1 and 25→1→25 sequences preserve counts/pagination; repeated same-limit requests reuse cached results.

findings.title: Malformed/duplicate M3U entries can silently select the wrong channel
findings.implementation: New EXTINF ends a malformed record; collision suffixes loop until unique; separate XMLTV identity maps programmes back to unique channel IDs.
findings.verification: Missing URL cannot steal next stream; adversarial preexisting suffixes stay unique/stable; duplicate provider IDs retain guide association without mutating original programmes.

findings.title: Highlight segment metadata grows without bound even though media files wrap
findings.implementation: FFmpeg segment_list_size bounds completed metadata; snapshot work deduplicates bounded entries and excludes the active writer.
findings.verification: Actual FFmpeg lavfi produces 40 completed segments with wrap 4; manifest retains 3 ordered completed entries across wraps; export regressions preserve playback order.

findings.title: Backend tests inherit local integration settings and can call the network
findings.implementation: Tests strip inherited settings before app import, disable dotenv, use synthetic defaults and fail external DNS/sockets; multi-socket fixtures share one ASGI loop.
findings.verification: Full 736-test backend suite passes with blank JWT, invalid PORT, hostile upstream URL and synthetic parent credentials while external networking is denied; 53 shared-loop WebSocket tests pass.

coverage.assessment: MEDIA-03 enforces process/export quotas at the trusted process boundary. Current deployment uses one backend worker.
coverage.followup: Before increasing workers/replicas, move quotas to shared admission; operator must document intended exposure and enforce login/chat/WebSocket ingress budgets. Gateway configuration was outside this repository; existing exposure was not expanded.

coverage.assessment: SEC-04 rechecks admin policy; SEC-06 enforces actual JWT expiry. Existing client session IDs and Plex-owner compatibility policy remain.
coverage.followup: Design server-bound multi-tab presence and retain immutable Plex grant provenance before requiring immediate revocation. Seven-day stateless revocation latency is distinct from expired-socket authorization.

coverage.assessment: Added routed TVView/store scenarios, actual CastButton+hook SDK fixtures, HLS shared shortcuts and ownership races.
coverage.followup: Run physical Chromecast resume/replacement/reachability smoke tests on the intended network. SDK doubles establish lifecycle logic, not receiver interoperability.

coverage.assessment: Generated production worker runs in real Chrome; legacy account caches and live resources are tested. Removed duplicated-regex tautology coverage.
coverage.followup: Keep npm build + check-service-worker.mjs and --media as release integration checks; test upgrades from any future intentionally cached account data.

coverage.assessment: Deferred QR/auth/Cast completions, generation changes, native-focused targets and matching chat ACKs are covered.
coverage.followup: Maintain late-success/failure/cancel permutations when extending those APIs; current reviewed race acceptance criteria are covered.

coverage.assessment: Actual synthetic FFmpeg capture/conversion and Chrome fMP4/encrypted HLS playback now verified.
coverage.followup: Before platform support claims, exercise native Safari HLS, mobile autoplay/fullscreen, TV remote and sustained real-provider decoding. No live Plex/Dispatcharr/ErsatzTV or physical receiver validation was performed.

coverage.assessment: FE-12 advances programme metadata; no measured evidence established a guide rendering performance defect.
coverage.followup: Profile realistic large guide fixtures and a multi-day open session, including the mount-fixed 48-hour horizon, before selecting moving windows/virtualization.

coverage.assessment: Focused control handling is repaired; no-CORS animated-image canvas fallback behavior remains a separate unconfirmed coverage gap.
coverage.followup: Use controlled cross-origin animated images in Chrome/Safari to verify pause/replay/reduced-motion; decide a static fallback if freezing cannot be supported.

coverage.assessment: Status shape/error isolation is fixed; no change to Plex OAuth error contract was required for the confirmed fixes.
coverage.followup: Add HTML200, malformed user/resources, timeout and DNS fixtures to normalize Plex auth errors into stable retryable responses without weakening validation.

coverage.assessment: Release scanning stages remain, builds get unique IDs and deployment pins/scopes artifact identity.
coverage.followup: Operator should confirm branch protection/pre-merge CI and pin mutable actions/base/installer provenance as policy requires; perform current vulnerability/image scans. This remediation is not an advisory clearance.

coverage.assessment: Host critical section includes verification; current/previous digest and compose records support explicit recovery. Optional upstreams remain outside process liveness.
coverage.followup: Rehearse documented manual rollback under the same lock on the real host; choose whether automatic rollback/readiness gates are desired. No production deployment or rollback was executed.

coverage.assessment: Retained HLS helpers now use bounded bodies, origin-checked redirects and manifest header validation.
coverage.followup: Cast internal filename helper has no demonstrated external traversal because route takes one segment; consolidate containment before exposing any additional multi-component filename entry point.

coverage.assessment: MEDIA-13 handles malformed boundaries/colliding IDs and preserves XMLTV identity; Ersatz parser failures retain stale cache with backoff.
coverage.followup: Add actual provider fixtures for remaining XMLTV timezone/episode/DefusedXML cases and Dispatcharr URL variants. No successful XXE was asserted or exercised.

coverage.assessment: Immutable snapshots/export sources and bounded metadata are tested using synthetic media. Packet clock/GOP/provider topology remain deployment-specific.
coverage.followup: Test clock jumps/keyframe boundaries and document desired trim precision; verify Cast URLs are receiver-reachable on LAN or remote topology before enabling it. Snapshot creation briefly pauses its Linux recorder; MP4 uses stream copy.

coverage.assessment: Media admission is associated with authenticated identity. Existing known-UUID stop/playback capability behavior is preserved.
coverage.followup: If creator-only stop or immediate capability revocation is required, introduce that explicit product contract and tests. Possession of the currently intended UUID capability is not newly labelled an authorization bypass.

coverage.assessment: DEV-01 and SEC-02 repair tested setup, relative APIs, generated signing keys and disabled blank accounts; obsolete credential/env comments removed.
coverage.followup: Operating limits are recorded below. Keep examples synchronized with the tested same-origin startup path and document physical network/device prerequisites when validated.
